# Ship Orbital Support Weapons
## Command: Arming the Ship Open the ship weapons arming terminal with command access. Choose [bold]at least one different weapon, up to the limit displayed by the terminal[/bold] and confirm. The default limit is three. [color=red]Confirmation permanently locks the entire loadout for the operation. Picking fewer than the limit does not leave slots available for later.[/color] Each selected weapon has [bold]three fire missions[/bold]. More terminals, batteries, or ammunition cannot reset those uses. Each ship has its own loadout, uses, and cooldown. Decks in one ship's Z-level network share them; identical ships do not.
## Loading Physical Batteries When the server requires physical guns, a compatible anchored battery must be installed on your ship before command can arm its weapons. It need not be loaded during arming, but firing requires a matching loaded mission round. - [bold]Heavy battery[/bold]: 120mm HE, 380mm HE, Airburst. - [bold]Support projector[/bold]: Gas, EMS, Smoke. - [bold]Rapid battery[/bold]: Gatling, Walking, Precision. - [bold]Railcannon[/bold]: Railcannon Strike. Use a compatible round on the gun to load it. Alt-click or use its eject verb to unload. Each gun holds one round. [bold]One round supplies the entire mission[/bold], including every barrage shell. A gun loaded with one supported weapon's round cannot fire another weapon's mission. When physical guns are not required, arming and firing work without batteries or rounds. This is the default server setting.
## Overwatch: Calling a Strike Use the existing orbital bombardment tab, enter ground coordinates, select an armed weapon, and confirm fire. Walking Barrage also lets you choose its travel direction. The first impact arrives [bold]24 seconds after launch[/bold]. A shared [bold]60-second cooldown[/bold] starts when the ship accepts a launch. Nearby troops receive the launch warning, then [bold]one directional warning three seconds later[/bold] pointing from their position toward the target. A final-approach warning precedes impact. Rejected targets, missing rounds, cooldown failures, and depleted weapons consume nothing. Accepted launches spend one use and, when required, one round immediately. Protection changes can intercept later impacts without a refund. The standard orbital cannon remains separate, with its existing ammunition, fuel, and cooldown.
## Strike Profiles Scatter is the maximum distance between the requested target and an individual impact. Its blast radius extends beyond that point. - [bold]Gatling Barrage[/bold]: 120 small explosions, 0.15 seconds apart, scattered within 16 tiles. Each has a 1.5-tile blast radius. - [bold]Walking Barrage[/bold]: 9 HE explosions, one second apart, moving along a 16-tile line centered on the target. Each has a 6-tile blast radius. - [bold]120mm HE Barrage[/bold]: 12 explosions, 0.75 seconds apart, scattered within 16 tiles. Each has a 12-tile blast radius. - [bold]380mm HE Barrage[/bold]: 6 heavy explosions, 1.8 seconds apart, scattered within 6 tiles. Each has a 16-tile blast radius. - [bold]Airburst Strike[/bold]: 6 anti-personnel explosions, 0.8 seconds apart, scattered within 8 tiles. Each has a 12-tile blast radius, without breaking terrain tiles. - [bold]Precision Strike[/bold]: one 120mm-strength explosion at the exact target, with a 12-tile blast radius and no scatter. - [bold]Railcannon Strike[/bold]: devastating whole-body and structural damage in an exact 5x5 tile square, projected through [bold]every Z-level in the target's network[/bold]. Each level retains orbital-protection checks; unrelated maps are not hit. - [bold]Gas Strike[/bold]: a 30-tile-radius poison cloud lasting 30 seconds. Xenos take no gas damage. Suitable filters and sealed internals provide their normal protection. - [bold]EMS Strike[/bold]: a 30-tile-radius field lasting 15 seconds. Everyone caught, including xenos and normally stun-immune targets, stays stunned until 25 seconds after the field disappears. Entering late or leaving early does not change that deadline. - [bold]Smoke Strike[/bold]: a non-damaging, opaque 30-tile-radius screen lasting 30 seconds.
[color=red]These expanded barrages can reach beyond the standard OB footprint. Keep friendly forces clear of both the scatter area and each shell's blast radius.[/color]
